newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Kelantan signs $800 mln petrochem deal.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Kelantan signs $800 mln petrochem deal.

text.p: Malaysia's only opposition-ruled state, Kelantan, on Friday signed a deal with KUB Malaysia Bhd, a government-backed cooperative, to build a two billion ringgit ($800 million) petrochemical complex.

Few details were avaiable on the agreement between Kelantan state-owned Keloil Sdn Bhd and KUB, which was witnessed by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and the state Chief Minister Nik Aziz of the fundamentalist Parti Islam se-Malaysia (PAS).
Officials of PAS, which administers Kelantan, said the project will help in the economic recovery of the state.
Kelantan is one of the poorest of Malaysia's 13 states.

In a statement, KUB said the project will involve the construction of an "integrated industrial and commercial park which will facilitate the utilitsation, processing, distributiuon and development of petroleum resources and products".

"Our immediate task is to acquire about 5,000 acres of land from Kelantan landowners for the plant which will be built over five years," Hassan Harun, chairman of KUB, told reporters before signing the deal.
"We can't reveal further details on the project until then," he added.
